article_title: A uniform bound of five for Diophantine tuples in imaginary quadratic integer rings

before.name: No Diophantine sextuples in rings of integers of imaginary quadratic fields
before.description:
## Overview

A Diophantine tuple, or $D(1)$-tuple, in a commutative ring with identity is a finite set of nonzero elements such that $ab+1$ is a square in the ring whenever $a$ and $b$ are distinct elements of the set. This project formalizes a uniform bound for $D(1)$-tuples in the full rings of integers of imaginary quadratic number fields. Every such tuple has at most five elements.

## Mathematical setting

Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic number field, that is, an extension of $\mathbb Q$ of degree two that admits no embedding into $\mathbb R$. Let $\mathcal O_K$ denote its full ring of integers, consisting of the elements of $K$ that are integral over $\mathbb Z$.

A finite set $S\subseteq\mathcal O_K\setminus\{0\}$ is a $D(1)$-tuple if
$$
\forall a,b\in S,\quad a\ne b\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists r\in\mathcal O_K,\quad r^2=ab+1.
$$
The value $ab+1=0$ is allowed, with $r=0$. Requiring the square roots to lie in $K$ instead of $\mathcal O_K$ gives the same notion, since $\mathcal O_K$ is integrally closed in $K$.

## Main theorem

For every imaginary quadratic number field $K$ and every $D(1)$-tuple $S$ in $\mathcal O_K$,
$$
|S|\le 5.
$$
Equivalently, $\mathcal O_K$ contains no $D(1)$-tuple with six elements.

[Adžaga](https://doi.org/10.1142/S1664360719500206) established a uniform bound of $42$. Cipu and Fujita established bounds of [$24$ in 2024](https://doi.org/10.1112/blms.12929) and [$22$ in 2026](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00605-026-02233-y). Whether a $D(1)$-tuple with five elements exists in the ring of integers of any imaginary quadratic field remains an open question ([Dujella, Problem 1.11](https://web.math.pmf.unizg.hr/~duje/pdf/open2.pdf)).

## Scope

The theorem concerns the full ring of integers in every case. In particular, for a positive squarefree integer $d\equiv3\pmod4$, it applies to $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})$, whose ring of integers strictly contains $\mathbb Z[\sqrt{-d}]$. No further hypotheses are imposed on the entries.

## Lean formalization

The Lean 4 development `D1Bound5` uses mathlib's full ring of integers `𝓞 K`. Its main declaration is `D1Bound5.main_statement`, whose type is `D1Bound5.MainStatement`.

The proposition `D1Bound5.MainStatement` quantifies over types `K` with instances `Field K`, `NumberField K` and `NumberField.IsTotallyComplex K`, subject to `Module.finrank ℚ K = 2`, and over finite sets `A : Finset (𝓞 K)`. It asserts `A.card ≤ 5` whenever `D1Bound5.IsD1 A` holds. The definition `D1Bound5.IsD1` requires every member to be nonzero and, for distinct members `x` and `y`, a witness `r` in the same ring satisfying `r * r = x * y + 1`.

## Reference and source code

Zrinka Franušić and Tomislav Pejković, *[A uniform bound of five for Diophantine tuples in imaginary quadratic integer rings](https://github.com/tomislav-math/diophantine-tuples-bound-five)*, preprint, 2026.

[Lean formalization](https://github.com/tomislav-math/d1-bound5-lean)
